# Dialing in espresso at home

Dialing in espresso means adjusting grind size, dose and shot time until the cup tastes balanced. Most home baristas start with 18 grams of ground coffee and aim for about 36 grams of liquid in the cup after 25 to 30 seconds, then change one setting at a time and taste every shot.

A burr grinder matters more than the espresso machine for most beginners. Burrs crush the beans to an even size, so water flows through the puck at a steady rate. Blade grinders leave a mix of dust and chunks, and that mix makes the same recipe taste sour one morning and bitter the next.

Fresh beans also change how a shot behaves. Coffee roasted within the last two to four weeks releases more gas, which slows the flow and builds crema. Older beans flow faster at the same grind, so a recipe that worked last month may need a finer setting today to reach the same time.

- Grind finer
- Dose more

> "Taste first," says the roaster.
